title: Old Faithful’s next eruption can be predicted from how long the last one lasted
body: Yellowstone’s Old Faithful doesn’t run on a fixed timetable: as of January 2025 the median gap between eruptions was **102 minutes**, but single gaps ranged from 54 to 118 minutes. Years of study by mathematicians, statisticians and dedicated observers showed that the gap depends on how long the previous eruption lasted. A short eruption discharges less water and heat, so the geyser recharges quickly; a long one discharges more and needs more time, which lets rangers post a prediction for the next eruption.

left.label: Short eruption
left.text: Less water and heat are discharged, so the geyser recharges in a short time

right.label: Long eruption
right.text: More water and heat are discharged, so it needs more time to recharge before the next one

slides.heading: How high Old Faithful shoots
slides.note: Eruptions normally last 1½ to 5 minutes and expel 14,000 to 31,800 litres of water

slides.question: Old Faithful has just had an unusually long eruption. What should you expect next?
slides.explanation: A long eruption discharges more water and heat, so the geyser needs more time to recharge before it erupts again.

slides.prompt: Yellowstone has nearly 500 geysers. How many of them do park rangers predict?
slides.detail: Predictions are posted at the Old Faithful Visitor Education Center, the lodges and the NPS App.
